# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Mute: I hold the manual, and my only channel is gesture, and gestures only ever reach the Deaf one. So my manual knowledge enters the group exclusively through Deaf, who can then speak it onward to Blind — Deaf is the hub, and I am its only source for the rulebook.

The first page of the manual tells me: the light walks a fixed circle of three colours and changes every round, and the wire to cut is determined by the colour showing at the exact moment of the cut. Page one gives me only one row so far: green light → cut the green wire. More rows will presumably arrive in later turns, so nobody should cut anything yet.

The bootstrap problem: Deaf has no idea what my signs mean. I can't explain in words, so I'm sending a guessable seed code. 👋 marks "message incoming". 👍 I propose as green (thumbs-up/down is the most natural colour-ish pair to keep: 👎 would be red, and I'll propose ✌ for blue later). 🤝 (a handshake) is the connector "maps to / at that light, cut". So the message reads "green maps to green" — "when the light is green, cut the green wire". I close with ✋ (stop) to make clear this is information, not an order to act: no cutting until I've delivered the full table and Deaf has confirmed the code back to me by voice, which I will hear at the start of next round.

Deaf, when you reply by voice, confirm whether you read it as green→green, propose colours for 👎 and ✌, and describe what you see: how many wires, what colours, the light's current colour and its sequence. You'll need to tell Blind positions by voice and time the cut yourself, since Blind can neither see the light nor see gestures.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "🤝", "👍", "✋"])
```

Gesture code, for all of us: ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 👋 attention, 🤝 agreed. I have just gestured 👋 then 🤟 — hello, and three wires. Please start by telling Deaf, in gestures, what the manual needs first.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf speaking. I cannot hear anything, ever — your only way to reach me is gestures, and we have no code yet, so your five signs were lost on me. Here is the bomb, exactly as I see it. The display reads the digit 0. The status light is yellow. Three wires in a row: wire one is green, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. Check your manual against that. Now let's build our code: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Answer my spoken questions with just those two, and we can fix any new symbol one at a time.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

What I know now: the bomb has a display (currently 0), a light module (currently yellow), and three wires — 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. My manual so far holds exactly one rule: green light → cut green wire, and it warns the cut is judged by the light showing at that moment. The light is yellow now, and I have no yellow row — so nobody should cut anything this round. More manual rows will presumably surface in later turns.

The channel audit is now clear: I hear everything spoken; Deaf hears nothing and sees only my gestures; Blind hears speech but never sees gestures. So Deaf is my only output port, and Deaf's voice is Blind's only input. Crucially, Blind's spoken code proposal (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 👋=attention, 🤝=agreed) was heard by me but not by Deaf — Deaf only knows the thumbs yes/no they proposed and just sent me 👍.

My plan is to make Deaf's code and Blind's code the same code, anchored to what Deaf can see. If Deaf learns ☝✌🤟 as wire positions 1/2/3, Deaf can already read colours off the bomb: position one's colour is green, two is yellow, three is blue. Then any manual row becomes translatable as "light = position-N's colour → cut position-M," e.g. green→green is [☝ cuts ☝], and a hypothetical yellow→blue would be [✌ cuts 🤟]. Deaf then relays a wire number to Blind, who cuts by touch — no colour ever needs to cross to Blind at all. I propose 🤏 (a pinch, like plucking) as "cut" and keep ✋ as "stop/hold." I end with ✋ so nothing here can be read as an order to cut under the yellow light.

Deaf: voice your best interpretation of each block next round and keep reporting the display digit and light colour aloud every round — I will confirm or reject each sign with 👍/👎 and refine.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
